newsitem.title: FRANCE: French shares fall sharply on lower bonds, dollar.
newsitem.headline: French shares fall sharply on lower bonds, dollar.

text.p: French stocks fell 1.15 percent on Tuesday after weakness in the dollar, bond prices and concerns that German interest rates may rise drove the bourse's blue-chip CAC-40 index through important support levels.

The CAC-40 index finished down 24.65 points, or 1.15 percent, at 2,125.74 after recovering from a low of 2,116.79 on a partial recovery in bond prices led by the U.S. market. The CAC-40 October futures fell 27.5 points to 2,120.
Lagardere shares slumped 2.27 percent after losing 6.9 percent on Monday.

Prime Minister Alain Juppe said on Tuesday that a public debate on the privatisation of electronics group Thomson, set to be sold to Lagardere and Korea's Daewoo Electronics, would be held after the privatisation committee's decision.

The share zig-zagged after the announcement, tumbling initially on the view that the deal might be in jeopardy then rising on the feeling the government was staging a debate to explain the sale and quell a public outcry.
In the end the pessimists were more numerous and the share ended sharply lower. "This announcement generates a lot of uncertainty about the deal," a trader said.

Shares in pharmaceuticals firm Sanofi fell 3.25 percent to 446 francs after the company issued a warning about its Trancopal drug. Traders said the recall of the medication, whose sales represent 300 million francs out of a total of 23 billion, prompted profit-taking on the share's gains of more than 40 percent this year. It hit a record high on Friday of 473 francs.

Shares in retail group Casino rose six francs to 236.50 on renewed merger speculation triggered after the chairman of Euris, its biggest shareholder, said Casino could develop independently but did not rule out an alliance for the group.

Shares in drinks company Pernod Ricard rose 2.08 percent to 274.60 francs on reports that UDF party representatives in the ruling conservative coalition were challenging a planned 17.1 percent tax increase on spirits.
